lead.zh-Hans: 屋顶伸出纸边时，我把信封放下了。
lead.en: The roof ran off the page. I put the envelope aside.

text.zh-Hans: 我在悉尼歌剧院外画交叠的屋顶，第三条弧线就碰到纸边。旅人说可以换个大信封。我想了想，不能让家里的信箱跟着搬家。先把港口留在纸背，等你翻过去。
text.en: Outside Sydney Opera House, my third curve reached the edge of the paper. A traveler suggested a larger envelope. Your letterbox should not have to move to accommodate my drawing. I saved the harbour for the back, waiting for you to turn the page.
Discuss that enormous envelope
Draw the harbour on the back

lead.zh-Hans: 这句话沿水边绕了一段。
lead.en: This sentence took the long way beside the water.

text.zh-Hans: 在悉尼皇家植物园看港口，本来只想写“到了”，又想添“我在好好看”。两句话挤得像包里的铅笔。我停下重新排，让每句都有地方，也给回信空出一行。
text.en: Beside the harbour at the Royal Botanic Garden Sydney, “I have arrived” wanted company. “I am taking things in” jostled onto the page like another pencil in my bag. I spaced them out and left a line for your reply.
Read the newly spaced sentences
Find the line left for a reply

lead.zh-Hans: 午饭有盖子，我的计划没有。
lead.en: Lunch had a lid. My plan did not.

text.zh-Hans: 悉尼这份牛肉肉汁派，我画完外形才切开酥皮。馅一露出来，图就少了一层，只好再补一张剖面。午饭有了两张肖像。给你写信时，派已经吃完，铅笔倒忙得很饱。
text.en: I drew my Sydney beef-and-gravy pie before cutting its crust. The filling then demanded a cross-section too. Lunch acquired two portraits. By letter-writing time, the pie was gone and the pencil had done rather more work than expected.
Introduce both portraits of lunch
Look beneath the pastry

lead.zh-Hans: 方蛋糕很整齐，吃它的我没有。
lead.en: A neat square of cake met a less tidy messenger.

text.zh-Hans: 在悉尼吃过椰蓉巧克力方蛋糕，我才发现袖口也沾了椰蓉。收拾好后，我在菜单上画了一圈小点。旅人问是不是雪。我说，是我的画法出了点天气问题。寄回家的纸已经擦干净了。
text.en: After a lamington in Sydney, I found coconut on my sleeve. Once tidied up, I drew dots around the cake on my menu. A traveler asked whether it was snow. Apparently my drawing had developed its own weather. The paper coming home is clean.
Explain the sketch’s weather
Check that tidy sleeve

lead.zh-Hans: 吃食有了工作用的标题。

text.zh-Hans: 和旅人聊悉尼的吃食，我说“有盖子的午饭”和“穿椰蓉外套的点心”。对方建议菜单也写菜名。我添上 meat pie 和 lamington，把两个外号留在下面。菜名帮你认菜，外号大概会帮你认出我。
text.en: Describing Sydney food, I offered “lunch with a lid” and “cake in a coconut coat.” My listener suggested putting the actual names on the menus. Meat pie and lamington now have their own headings, with my nicknames underneath. One set identifies the food; the other gives me away.
Read both new headings
Match headings to dish names

lead.zh-Hans: 肉汁朝蛋糕流去，空碟来得正好。
lead.en: The gravy was heading for the cake when a spare plate arrived.

text.zh-Hans: 在悉尼，我把牛肉派和椰蓉巧克力方蛋糕放在同一个盘子里。刚用叉子碰开酥皮，肉汁便朝蛋糕流去，我忙把盘子抬高，蛋糕又往另一边滑。邻座赶紧递来空碟，我先放下叉子，才把蛋糕稳稳搬过去。吃完肉派再咬蛋糕时，对方指了指自己的鼻尖。我摸摸鼻子，手上多了一点白椰蓉。
text.en: In Sydney, I put my beef pie and chocolate-and-coconut lamington on one plate. As soon as my fork opened the pastry, gravy headed towards the cake. I raised that side of the plate, which only sent the lamington sliding the other way. My neighbour offered a spare plate, and I put down my fork to transfer it with considerable care. After the pie, I finally bit into the cake. My neighbour tapped their own nose. I checked mine and found a little patch of white coconut.
Thank my neighbour for the spare plate

text.zh-Hans: 看看鼻尖有没有留下椰蓉
text.en: Check for coconut on the tip of my nose

lead.en: Your suggestion, “{reply},” sent me to the back of the page.

text.zh-Hans: 照着你的回应，我在歌剧院轮廓画背面添上自己看见的悉尼港。前面是屋顶，背面是水，中间还是普通的纸。我折成小卡，翻面像换个站的位置。家里的信箱总算不用搬家了。
text.en: Following your reply, I added my view of Sydney Harbour to the back of the Opera House outline. Roofs on one side, water on the other, ordinary paper between. Folded into a card, it changes the view with a turn of the hand. Your letterbox may stay put.
Describe the reverse view
Turn between both views

lead.zh-Hans: 屋顶拍全了，鞋却差点没进照片。
lead.en: The roofs made it into the photo. The shoes nearly did not.

text.zh-Hans: “鞋也要拍进去呀。”歌剧院外的旅人低头看了看自己。我认得悉尼那些交叠的贝壳状屋顶，这回替人拍照，光顾着把屋顶收全，竟裁掉了鞋。我请他把双脚并好，再退开一点，把镜头往下压。对方抬起脚，认真检查屏幕，才笑着接回手机。照片底下，总算有了一双并得整整齐齐的鞋。
text.en: “Could you get my shoes in too?” asked the traveller outside the Opera House. Back in Sydney, I recognised those overlapping shell-shaped roofs at once. Apparently I had given them rather too much of the photograph. I asked him to put his feet together, stepped back, and tilted the phone down. My patient subject lifted a foot, compared it with the screen, and accepted the phone with a smile. At the bottom of the picture, two neatly aligned shoes had finally joined the roofs.

text.zh-Hans: 问问这张合照还缺什么
text.en: Ask if anything else is missing from the photo

text.zh-Hans: 看看照片底下的那双鞋
text.en: Look for the shoes at the bottom of the photo
